title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 50 of the continuation of La Longue Marche begins a worked example, 'la tour de Fermat'. It is the abelian (Fermat-curve) tower over P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, seen through the modular group.

Setting. Let G_0^ be the profinite completion of SL(2,Z), with generators rho (order 6) and sigma (order 4), rho^3 = sigma^2 = -1. Let Pi_0 be the free subgroup of rank 2 generated by lambda_i = -l_i, where l_0 = [[1,-2],[0,1]] and l_1 = [[1,0],[2,1]]. Concretely Pi_0 = {g in Gamma(2) : a = d = 1 mod 4}, so Gamma(2) = {+-1} x Pi_0. Pi_0 is the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, realised as the Legendre / level-2 modular curve. It has index 12, is normal in SL(2,Z), and contains Gamma(4).

The extension. Dividing by [Pi_0,Pi_0], which is characteristic in Pi_0 and hence normal, gives an extension (2): 1 -> M -> G -> H -> 1. Here:
- M = Pi_0^ab = (Z^(0) + Z^(1) + Z^(infinity)) / diagonal. This is the free profinite abelian group on the inertia generators at the three cusps, modulo the single relation that they sum to zero.
- H = G_0/Pi_0 has order 12 and is identified with SL(2,Z/4) divided by the images of the level-4 classes.
- Since Gamma(4) is contained in Pi_0, H is a quotient of SL(2,Z/4).
- The full group G actually used (cf. next page) is GL(2,Z)^/[Pi_0,Pi_0]. It contains an extra involution tau', and G/M = S_3 x mu_2, which Grothendieck identifies with the Teichmueller group T_{0,3}.
- Finite levels of the extension are the automorphism groups of the Fermat curves, (Z/n)^2 extended by S_3 (times ±1).

Presentation (3). G = <tau', rho, sigma | rho^6 = sigma^4 = tau'^2 = 1, rho^3 = sigma^2, tau' rho tau'^-1 = rho^-1, tau' sigma tau'^-1 = sigma^-1, [lambda_0, lambda_1] = 1>. The words are lambda_0 = -sigma rho sigma rho = sigma(rho) rho and lambda_1 = -rho sigma rho sigma = rho sigma(rho), where x(y) = x y x^-1. This presents the discrete group; G is its completion. One commutator relation suffices because Pi_0 is free on lambda_0, lambda_1, so [Pi_0,Pi_0] is the normal closure of [lambda_0, lambda_1].

Rewriting the relation. (4): sigma(rho) rho^2 sigma(rho) = rho sigma(rho^2) rho. Using rho^2 = -rho^-1 and sigma^-1 = -sigma, this becomes (5): -sigma (rho sigma rho^-1 sigma rho) sigma = (rho sigma rho^-1 sigma rho). The braced word is lambda_infinity, as defined on the next page. So the relation that lambda_0 and lambda_1 commute is equivalent to [sigma, lambda_infinity] = 1, i.e. sigma centralises the parabolic generator at infinity modulo [Pi_0,Pi_0]. Grothendieck then begins a remark on how to suppress the sign -1 in a pure generators-and-relations formalism: replace an odd number of sigma's by sigma^-1.

Purpose. The following pages build a discrete arithmetic model of M, namely M = Z^{0,1,infinity}/diagonal, with the canonical lattice points lambda_0 + lambda_1 + lambda_infinity = 0. S_3 x mu_2 acts on it by permuting and negating the lambda_i. The previous page proved a theorem on the algebraic/pro-algebraic envelope Ext_S(G) of a discrete group over a base S. The aim is to give a concrete instance of that envelope, and of the Teichmueller-group formalism, for the metabelian quotient of pi_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} together with its modular symmetries.
errors: Sign slip in (3): sigma rho sigma rho = sigma(rho) rho^4 = l_0, so lambda_0 = -sigma rho sigma rho equals sigma(rho) rho, not sigma(rho) rho^4. The slip is harmless for (4), since the signs cancel in the commutator.

H is written SL(2,Z/4)/(l_0, l_1) (dotted). The subgroup generated by the images of l_0 and l_1 is not normal in SL(2,Z/4): T conjugates I+2E21 to I+2(I+E12+E21). The correct normal subgroup is generated by the images of lambda_0 = -l_0 and lambda_1 = -l_1, i.e. the image of Pi_0. The dots may intend this, but as written it is inaccurate.
Which of sigma rho sigma rho and rho sigma rho sigma equals l_0 versus l_1 depends on the matrix chosen for rho. With some choices the labels are swapped; this is only a convention issue.
(3) is a presentation of the discrete group GL(2,Z)/[Pi_0,Pi_0]. The profinite G is its completion, which the text leaves implicit.

ideas.what: Quotient of SL(2,Z)^ (or GL(2,Z)^) by the commutator subgroup of the free level subgroup Pi_0 = pi_1(P^1 minus {0,1,inf}), giving an extension of S_3 x mu_2 by M = Z^3/diagonal: the 'Fermat tower' group
ideas.modern_name: Metabelian quotient of pi_1(P^1 minus {0,1,inf}) / automorphism group of the Fermat tower; profinite Teichmueller group T_{0,3} modulo the second derived subgroup
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1985-86, 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'), Anderson, Coleman, Deligne on Fermat curves
ideas.where_published: Teichmueller tower / T_{0,3} viewpoint is in Esquisse d'un programme; the Fermat-tower example specifically is unsure

ideas.what: Identification Pi_0^ab = (Z(0)+Z(1)+Z(inf))/diagonal, with cusp inertia generators summing to zero
Presentation of GL(2,Z)/[Pi_0,Pi_0] by rho, sigma, tau' plus one commutator relation, rewritten as sigma commuting with lambda_infinity
ideas.modern_name: Explicit presentation of the metabelian modular quotient

ideas.what: H = SL(2,Z)/Pi_0 of order 12 as a quotient of SL(2,Z/4) (Gamma(4) contained in Pi_0)
ideas.modern_name: Level-4 description of the Legendre subgroup

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly studies the Fermat tower as the metabelian quotient of the modular group, with its S_3 x mu_2 (= T_{0,3}) symmetry. On the next page he begins a Z-form (arithmetic model) of the group. This is the same object Ihara used shortly after for Galois actions and Jacobi-sum power series. The example seems to be used to illustrate his 'algebraic envelope' theorem for discrete groups (previous page), a link to Ihara-Anderson-Coleman that is not in the literature.
missed.quote: Exemple : Le "tour" de Fermat ... M = Π_{0ab} ≃ (Ẑ(0)+Ẑ(1)+Ẑ(∞))/diagonale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early independent treatment of the Fermat tower within Grothendieck's anabelian/Teichmueller programme. It also suggests combining Ihara's Galois action on the metabelian quotient with a pro-algebraic (Z-scheme) envelope of the discrete group.

missed.claim: The relation [lambda_0, lambda_1] = 1 in GL(2,Z)/[Pi_0,Pi_0] is equivalent to [sigma, lambda_infinity] = 1: the order-4 elliptic element centralises the cusp-infinity parabolic modulo [Pi_0,Pi_0]. The next page adds the formula [l_0,l_1] = (sigma(rho) rho^-1)^3.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A small but neat explicit identity; it is likely elementary and rediscoverable.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished, explicit treatment of the Fermat tower and metabelian modular quotient in the Teichmueller-group setting, plausibly predating or independent of Ihara. The individual computations are elementary and the overall object is well studied since the mid-1980s.
transcription_corrections: The sentence about signs reads roughly: 'où le sens des signes — peu explicites dans le formalisme des gén. et rel. — : on supprime dans la formule ces signes, en remplaçant un (ou un nb impair) des σ de la formule par des σ^{-1}'. The transcription's duplicated line 'nouvelles [?] (ou un nb impair) des σ de' is spurious.
lambda_0 line: as written it reads 'σ(ρ)ρ^4'. Mathematically it should be σ(ρ)ρ; the '^4' may be a slip or relate to the top-margin annotation 'σρ^4'.
Line 1: 'Je m'intéresse au quotient de 𝔊_0^ = Sl(2,Ẑ)'; the hat is on 𝔊_0 (profinite completion).
Under M: 'Π_0 ab, ...' — the phrase after it is illegible; 'ind. sous 𝔊_0' is uncertain.
